Backlash refers to the angle that the output shaft of a gearhead can rotate without the input shaft moving. Backlash arises due to tolerance in manufacturing; the gear teeth need some play to avoid jamming when they mesh. An inexpensive gearhead may have backlash of a degree or more, while more expensive precision gearheads have nearly zero backlash.
